_comment: BAND-SPLIT. Band-local clusters for band5_stronghold_approach. `order` is this entry's index in the merged array and is the ONLY thing that decides merge position -- never file order, never band order. Existing entries keep the index they had before the split because the merged array order is the order props are added to the scene tree, and Godot silently auto-renames same-named siblings by that order. A new entry in this band takes an unused order in this band's reserved range 5000-5999, which no other band can collide with; do not renumber an existing one.
_comment_bare: BAND5-CONTENT. This file was empty and prompt 66 asks for visible Team Tether occupation building across the region, not just at the doorstep, plus a real final preparation point. Two clusters, both built from the same Quaternius Fantasy Props MegaKit every other band already uses (D24, one prop family) -- nothing new.

clusters.name: outer_watch_cache
clusters._why: The outer watch's own supply cache (trainers.json order 5005, Watchman Corr at (-68,7140)) -- a working checkpoint's kit, not an abandoned one: crates and a barrel stacked square and close together rather than scattered, the same 'a touching pile reads as one load' finding `quarry_station`'s own cluster (band2) already used, but upright and squared rather than tipped -- somebody here is still using it. A bag sits apart, ready rather than forgotten.

props._why: the cache's anchor, square to the road
stacked hard against the first crate's side -- a load, not a scatter
water for a post that expects to be manned a while
kit set down within arm's reach of the challenge line, not tucked away -- Corr is on duty, not camped

clusters.name: the_waystop
clusters._why: EXPEDITION-REST/prompt 66's final preparation point. A remembered clearing, not a hotel: `vegetation.json` (order 5000) keeps this 14m nook clear for a player to build in, `harvest.json` (orders 5001-5005) puts wood/stone/fiber within a few paces, and this cluster is the flavour that makes it read as a place travellers already stop rather than a bare lawn -- log seats and a kept pack, no bed and no fire ring (the shipped prop family has neither model; `ranger_camp`'s own note in band2 records the same substitution). Deliberately NOT collapsed or abandoned like `ranger_camp`: this is the last waystop before the Hall, still in use, the difference between a place something happened to and a place people keep choosing to stop.
clusters._why_vp5: VP5 visual-parity pass. The smith's anvil is the reason this stop exists, but the fire it should have gathered around was the dimmest in the chapter and the seating sat off at odd distances rather than tangential to it. Fire brightened, bench pulled tangential and closer, a second log seat added opposite it, and the anvil, bag and bucket regrouped in close around the fire so the working half of the camp (smith's tools) and the resting half (seats) both read as arranged around one focal flame. A small supply pair (barrel and crate) was added by the anvil, clear of the creature bed, so the smith's own stock has a place.

rest._why:
T5-CADENCE. Band 5 was the audit's most pointed camp/recovery FAIL, because of what this band is FOR: 'Three prop clusters, all 4-prop supply caches. No bed, no fire, no camp anywhere in band 5 -- and this is the band whose entire design purpose per FUN sec15 is final rest and preparation. The player's only option is to build one.'

THIS CLUSTER'S OWN `_why` ALREADY SAID SO, and its wording is what makes this addition an extension rather than a reversal: 'no bed and no fire ring (the shipped prop family has neither model; `ranger_camp`'s own note in band2 records the same substitution)'. That substitution is now spent -- `campfire_stone_ring.glb` and `camp_bed.glb` have both shipped from the owner-referenced camp set (docs/specs/ASSET_LEDGER.md) and are already placed in bands 1, 2, 3 and 4. Nothing is generated or sourced; the fire and the bed this waystop was authored to have and could not are simply available.

THE NOOK STAYS BUILDABLE, which is the one thing the cluster's own note asks for ('vegetation.json (order 5000) keeps this 14m nook clear for a player to build in'). Every piece added here hugs the existing bench/anvil group on the road side; the nook's centre and its western half are untouched. A player who wants their own camp here still has the ground for it, and a player who does not now has somewhere to sleep before the Hall.
rest.label: Rest until morning

creature_bed._why: The last creature bed before the Warden. FUN sec15 and VISION sec3 both ask for 'one last meaningful opportunity to prepare, rest, adjust the five' immediately before the climax, and until this the answer was 'build one'. Sited at (-21.0,7459.4) -- the flattest ground measured anywhere at this site (0.84m of relief over a 4m pad, against 1.3-1.6m everywhere else nearby), on the road side of the group and clear of the nook the vegetation mask keeps open.

props._why: the cluster's anchor -- seating, facing back down the road the player just climbed
props._why_vp5: VP5. Pulled tangential to the fire, 2.6m W of it -- the deeper sink (0.08) follows the ground rising to the west at this distance.

props._why: a second, lower seat opposite the bench -- two ways to sit, the same cue `ranger_camp`'s round 3 used for 'a place people actually gathered'. VP5: the smith's own anvil, the reason this waystop exists, moved in close by the fire rather than sitting apart from it
somebody's kit, set down and not forgotten -- whoever stopped here meant to come back for it, unlike the abandoned camps further back
props._why_vp5: VP5. Moved against the bench's own south end, the same touching-pile rule this chapter's other camps use.

props._why: within reach of the bench, not tipped -- this stop is tended
props._why_vp5: VP5. Moved beside the anvil -- water for the smith's own work, close enough to read as part of the same station.

props._why: T5-CADENCE. The fire ring this cluster's own `_why` records as unbuildable when it was authored ('the shipped prop family has neither model'). It is buildable now: the owner-referenced ring already committed under assets/props/generated_camp and already placed at four other sites. Scale 0.9 -- a waystop's fire, between band 1's rest camp (1.05) and a picket's brazier (0.5). Sited on the road side of the bench so the seating faces it and the nook behind stays clear for a player's own build.

T5-CADENCE. The fire in it, the same solved combination every other camp in the chapter uses (`Bonfire_Fire.obj`'s real `Fire` surface + `ignite()` + campfire_glow.gd's light, embers and smoke). On the final approach it does a second job the other fires do not: `stronghold_occupation.json` drains this ground and lights it with Team Tether's own braziers, so one ordinary warm fire on the road is the last thing here that belongs to the Meadows rather than to the people who took it.
props._why_vp5: VP5. This was the dimmest fire in the chapter, no `glow_scale` at all against neighbouring camps' 1.4-1.8. Set to 1.4 so the last fire before the Hall is legible as the focal point the smith's anvil, seats and supplies are now arranged around, without overplaying it against the Team Tether braziers this same site sits beside.

props._why: T5-CADENCE. Firewood beside the new fire, radial rather than tangential -- band 1's own rule, for the opposite reason its seats obey. Kenney's textured CC0 log, as at every other camp.
props._why_vp5: VP5. Re-aimed radial to the fire now that the bench has moved off this bearing.

props._why: VP5 round9, coordinator spec: 'logs and stones around' the fire, told asymmetrically. Set 0.7m from the existing firewood log so the two touch and read as one dropped stack rather than one lone log -- the road-facing Stool 4.6m off stays this camp's one unpaired seat, so the touching pair and the lone watcher sit on opposite sides of the same clearing rather than a matched ring.
VP5. A second seat, tangential to the fire 2.8m E, opposite the bench -- the bench alone read as one seat facing an empty fire; a camp used by more than one traveller needs somewhere else to sit.

VP5. A kept shelter for the last waystop before the Hall -- still in use, unlike the abandoned camps further back. The D1 owner-referenced tent mesh (already committed, no new generation), sized between band1's rest-camp tent (1.05) and band4's patrol tent (0.85).
VP5. A small supply pair by the anvil -- the smith's own stock, clear of the seating arc and the creature bed at (-21, 7459.4)
VP5. Set touching the barrel, one load rather than a scatter

VP5 round8. An unpaired seat at the clearing's own road-facing edge, 4.6m clear of the fire group and turned to bearing 75.6 -- straight up the spine at the outer works (8.0,7560.0), the Hall itself. Every other seat here faces the fire; this one turns the last stop before the climax toward what the player is about to walk into, the read the site's own name (a traveller's halt facing the road ahead) was still missing.

clusters.name: road_watch_drop
clusters._why: BAND5-DEADTRAVEL, and prompt 66's 'visible Team Tether occupation' asked for ACROSS the 680m rather than at the doorstep. The driven run measured a 123m stretch of the spine with nothing within reach; this is the first of the three beats placed into it, and the one that does the region's own job. Not a manned post -- Corr is 150m behind and Ness 130m ahead, and a third body here would spend a combat beat the prompt explicitly says not to spend before the stronghold. A supply DROP instead: a load left on the road for somebody who has not come for it yet. The occupation is present in the props even where nobody is standing, which is the whole read this leg was missing. Same Quaternius Fantasy Props MegaKit as the other two clusters (D24, one prop family).

props._why: set square to the road, the way a load is put down rather than dropped
hard against the first -- `quarry_station`'s own finding, that a touching pile reads as one load and a scattered one reads as debris
upright, closing the third side, so the drop has a shape from the road
one item set apart and ready to be picked up -- the cue that says somebody is coming back for this
